area.hero.h1: Heating and cooling repair in Glenview, IL
area.hero.lede: Furnaces, central air, heat pumps and boilers, for Glenview post-war houses, newer houses and townhomes at The Glen, older houses in The Park and the shops downtown. Family-owned since 1952, with the owner, Rob, still on the calls.

area.reviews.1.quote: In August, the upstairs AC unit stopped working. Rob was able to diagnose and repair the issue and topped up the coolant in both condenser units. He also gave me an estimate for the basement furnace, which I knew needed replacing, and why I was especially happy that he didn't think the upstairs system needed replacing. The quote was good - a lower estimate was for a less well-regarded brand…
area.reviews.2.quote: Rob from City & suburban was super kind and helpful with our furnace and air conditioner maintenance. We wanted to make sure everything was running smoothly before winter and after calling Rob, he was able to come out very quickly. A few months later, our natural gas company let us know that we needed some repairs done, and after a phone call to City & Suburban, they came out the…
area.reviews.3.quote: My furnace went out, so I contacted City and Suburban Heating and Cooling to set up an appointment to get it checked out. Rob, the service tech, showed up on time to help me out. He told me he had to change out one part to get it up and running again, which he did in a very timely manner. And, without breaking the bank.
area.reviews.4.quote: I’ve worked with City & Suburban Heating & Cooling since we lived in our condo in Lincoln Park, and now that we’ve moved to a single-family home, they continue to help us maintain our system. Rob has been especially helpful—always consistent, reliable, and easy to work with. It’s great having a company we can trust for both service and ongoing maintenance. Highly recommend!
area.scope.heading: The same repair costs differently in a post-war house, a townhome and a shop
area.scope.1.why: A 1950s house and a house at The Glen run different equipment, so the age and layout of the system change the job.
area.scope.2.why: Larger Glenview houses can run a furnace and AC for each floor, so a repair starts with finding which one has failed.
area.scope.3.why: Houses from around 1900, like those in The Park, can still heat with a boiler and radiators.
area.scope.4.why: At The Glen and in other townhome associations, rules on outdoor units and access shape the work.
area.scope.5.why: Shops and offices at The Glen Town Center and downtown run rooftop units, so roof access and business hours set the work.
area.scope.6.why: The biggest swing of all. Where the unit has years left, we say so.

area.buildings.heading: What heats and cools your Glenview building
area.buildings.1.title: Post-war house
area.buildings.1.body: A furnace with central air, in the basement or a utility room. The condenser sits beside the house.
area.buildings.2.title: Newer house or townhome
area.buildings.2.body: A furnace or heat pump with central air. Larger houses run one system per floor.
area.buildings.3.title: House from around 1900
area.buildings.3.body: Often a boiler and radiators, sometimes a furnace added later. Ductless is a common way to cool.
area.buildings.4.title: Shop or office
area.buildings.4.body: Rooftop units for the stores and offices at The Glen Town Center and downtown.

area.faq.heading: Glenview HVAC, answered
area.faq.1.q: Is the furnace in my post-war house worth repairing, or does it need replacing?
area.faq.2.q: Do you come out to Glenview from Chicago?
area.faq.3.q: Do you work on houses and townhomes at The Glen?
area.faq.4.q: Does HVAC work in Glenview need a permit?
area.faq.1.a: Often it's worth repairing. We diagnose first, and where the furnace has years left, we say so. Replacement is quoted only when the repair stops making sense.
area.cta.body: Have the make of your furnace or condenser to hand, and tell us what it's doing. At The Glen, mention your association's rules on outdoor units.

extras.faq.2.a: Yes. Glenview is on our service area list, about 12 miles north-west of the shop at 1225 N Cleaver St, and Rob runs the calls from there.
extras.faq.3.a: Yes. Furnaces, central air and heat pumps are on our list of services. In a townhome, tell us the association's rules on outdoor units when you call.
extras.faq.4.a: It depends on the job. The Village of Glenview takes permit applications online and inspects every permit it issues, mostly installs and replacements. Ask whoever quotes an install who pulls the permit.

permits.source: No permit graph: City of Chicago building permits (ydr8-5enu) stop at the city limits, and the Village of Glenview doesn't publish its permits as open data.
permits.village_data: Village of Glenview: permits applied for online (glenview.onlama.com) or at the Development Center; 2021 International Mechanical Code with Glenview amendments; every permit issued requires an inspection (residential inspections page). No open permit dataset found (searched 15 Oct 2026). City & Suburban: 0 in the Chicago file, all years.
